title: Band-9 Samples: Do you ever save money to buy special things? [Why/why not?]
passage_text: This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 13 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 2 Test 3 question: “Do you ever save money to buy special things? [Why/why not?]” Sample 1: Yes Female Male Absolutely, saving for special things is a habit I’ve developed over the years. I think it’s essential to have a well-thought-out financial plan, which includes setting aside money for particular goals. By doing so, I can strike a balance between meeting my immediate needs and preparing for future endeavors, such as upgrading my home or expanding my education. Sample 2: Yes Female Male Yes, I do save money for special purchases, primarily because I value financial discipline and long-term planning. By doing so, I can avoid impulsive spending and ensure that I only invest in items that truly matter to me. This practice not only helps me achieve my financial goals but also instills a sense of accomplishment and satisfaction when I finally obtain the desired object. Sample 3: Yes Female Male Yes, I frequently allocate funds for special items or experiences. I find that having a clear objective to work towards motivates me to be more frugal in my day-to-day spending. For instance, I may curtail impulsive purchases in order to accumulate the necessary resources for an upcoming trip or to invest in a high-quality piece of furniture. Sample 4: Yes Female Male Certainly, I save money for special acquisitions, mainly because I cherish the concept of delayed gratification. By postponing the satisfaction of owning a specific item, I can better appreciate its worth once I’ve obtained it. Moreover, this practice helps foster a sense of responsibility and self-control, enabling me to make well-informed decisions regarding my spending habits. Sample 5: Yes Female Male Absolutely, I set aside money for exceptional purchases as a way of maintaining a healthy relationship with money. By consciously saving for special items, I can indulge in my desires without jeopardizing my financial stability or succumbing to excessive consumerism. This balanced approach allows me to enjoy the finer things in life while still adhering to a responsible and sustainable financial plan. Sample 6: No Female Male No, I don’t typically save money for special purchases. Instead, I focus on maintaining a stable financial foundation by ensuring that my essential expenses are covered and I have a decent emergency fund. I believe that this approach helps me achieve a more balanced and stress-free lifestyle, without the pressure of constantly striving to acquire material possessions. Sample 7: No Female Male To be frank, I don’t usually save money with the purpose of buying specific items. Instead, I prioritize investing in long-term goals such as my education or retirement fund. By doing so, I can secure financial stability for my future and focus on personal growth, rather than getting caught up in the pursuit of material possessions that may only bring temporary satisfaction. Sample 8: No Female Male No, I don’t save money for buying special things. I adopt a minimalist lifestyle, which entails being content with what I have and avoiding the pursuit of materialistic desires. By prioritizing my needs over my wants, I can maintain a healthy financial balance and prevent the accumulation of unnecessary items in my life. Sample 9: No Female Male Frankly, I don’t set aside money for acquiring special items. My financial strategy revolves around investing in assets and long-term financial instruments, which can help me grow my wealth and achieve financial independence. As a result, I place more emphasis on making prudent investment choices rather than saving for expensive purchases. Sample 10: No Female Male No, I don’t reserve money with the intention of buying extraordinary items. I’m a firm believer in living for the moment and taking advantage of the present. I prefer to invest in experiences and events that bring me joy and create lasting memories, instead of waiting to accumulate funds for a specific purchase. This way, I can enjoy a dynamic and gratifying life, free from the constraints of material belongings.
